title: Curried Chicken Salad with Mango Chutney, Currants and Almonds
changes_from_base: Same gently poached chicken, but the dressing is spiced with bloomed curry powder, mango chutney, lime and yoghurt, with currants, toasted almonds and coriander.
summary: This spiced take follows the same gentle poaching method as our classic chicken salad, but the dressing is built on bloomed curry powder, mango chutney, lime and yoghurt, with currants, toasted almonds and coriander stirred through.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt, for the poaching water
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Poach the Chicken
steps.text: The chicken breasts go into the saucepan with the cold water, salt, bay leaves and peppercorns; heat over medium until the water reaches 75-80°C, with just a few small bubbles breaking at the edge rather than a boil. Lower the heat as far as it will go, cover, and poach for 15-20 minutes until a probe thermometer shows 74°C in the thickest part, the temperature at which the chicken is fully cooked through. Cooking it this gently rather than at a boil is what keeps the breast moist instead of dry and stringy.

steps.title: Cool and Chop
steps.text: Once lifted onto a board, the chicken needs about 15 minutes to cool before you handle it, which gives the juices time to redistribute through the meat. After that, pull or chop it into 1-2 cm pieces that will hold their shape once mixed with the dressing.

steps.title: Bloom the Curry Powder
steps.text: Warm the oil in the small frying pan over low heat, stir in the curry powder, and cook it for 30-60 seconds until it smells fragrant rather than dusty. Tip it straight into the large bowl; warming spices briefly in fat like this wakes up their flavour in a way raw spices never quite manage. Using the same pan, toast the flaked almonds for 3 minutes, shaking often, until golden.

steps.title: Build the Dressing
steps.text: Into the curry-infused oil goes the mayonnaise, yoghurt, mango chutney, lime juice and salt, stirred until smooth. The yoghurt keeps the dressing light while the chutney brings sweetness and a little acidity that balances the warmth of the curry powder.

steps.title: Mix in the Chicken
steps.text: Fold the chopped chicken, celery, spring onion and currants through the dressing until everything is evenly coated. The currants plump up slightly as they sit in the dressing, adding small bursts of sweetness between the savoury bites.

steps.title: Chill and Garnish
steps.text: A minimum of 1 hour in the fridge, covered, gives the curry flavour time to settle through the salad. Just before serving, scatter over the toasted almonds and chopped coriander for crunch and a fresh, herby lift.

tips: Check the chicken reaches 74°C in the thickest part with a probe thermometer before taking it off the heat.
Common mistake: adding curry powder straight into the cold dressing — warming it briefly in oil first brings out far more flavour.
Chop any large pieces of mango chutney before stirring it in, so you don't end up with uneven pockets of sweetness.
Toast the almonds just before serving rather than too far ahead, as they lose their crunch if they sit too long.
Let the chicken cool before mixing it into the dressing, or the yoghurt and mayonnaise can thin out from the heat.
storage: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 3 days. It's not suitable for freezing, as the yoghurt and mayonnaise dressing will separate once thawed. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
